text:
maya: Heads up — noticed a CPU spike on collector workers right after we flipped the exporter TLS rollout last night. p95 looks stable but p99 tokenization latency +30% and sys CPU on the exporter pods jumped.

dan: Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/exporter-ops — spikes at 23:12 UTC :eyes:

infra-bot: deploy "enable-per-tenant-tls" promoted to canary (5%) at 2027-11-03T23:08:02Z

nina: did the rollout enable per-tenant cert rotation? that can cause sockets to drop and force new TLS handshakes if keepalives are short

leo: adding logs from one of the hot pods — lots of `TIME_WAIT` and short-lived connections:
```
netstat -an | grep 4317 | awk '{print $6}' | sort | uniq -c
  120 TIME_WAIT
   45 ESTABLISHED
  300 CLOSE_WAIT
```

rachel: flame graph points to openssl_do_handshake / SSL_do_handshake being hot during the window. looks like we do a handshake per RPC stream.

maya: config snippet from the collector canary (we enabled cert rotation):
```
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: collector.redwood-internal:4317
    tls:
      cert_rotation: true
      rotate_interval: 5m
    connection:
      max_idle: 30s
      keepalive: 15s
```

maya: hypothesis: cert rotation + short `max_idle`/keepalive + our current batching causing many short streams => TLS handshake cost at scale.

nina: makes sense. when streams are short (we open per-batch), handshake is amortized poorly. two quick mitigations: increase `max_idle` and keepalive, or multiplex via HTTP/2 (fewer handshakes).

leo: also seeing `tls_handshakes_total` metric climb on exporter side; adding it to the dashboard now.

rachel: another knob: increase batch window slightly so each stream carries more spans (trade latency for CPU). for low-traffic tenants that will help a lot.

maya: i'm going to push a canary patch that increases `max_idle` to 5m and `keepalive` to 60s, and bump batch window from 20ms to 80ms for the collector canary group (5%). will monitor p99 and cpu.

dan: please also add an alert for handshake rate > 1000/min per cluster. :face_with_monocle:

infra-bot: new canary config deployed to collector-canary-3 at 2027-11-03T23:26:10Z

maya: early results (5m after change): p99 latency down ~12%, CPU down ~18%, tls_handshakes_total dropped by ~70% on canary pods.

nina: nice. can we make the change global after a short bake? any downside to longer keepalives with cert rotation enabled?

rachel: main downside: if certs rotate frequently, long-lived connections might be using rotated-out certs — but we have server-side session revalidation. still do a gradual rollout and ensure revoke path works.

leo: follow-ups:
- add `tls_handshake_rate` panel to perf dashboard
- add a per-route connection usage graph
- run a mem/FD audit for long-lived connections

maya: i'll open a short doc with steps and the canary metrics, and schedule a 30m bake. plan to roll to 50% after 1h if stable.

dan: please tag platform-oncall during the next roll.

maya: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:

rachel: long-term idea: move exporter->collector to HTTP/2 with connection pooling at the SDK layer so we seldom pay handshake costs. track as a tech debt ticket.

maya: noted. created ticket INF-9836 "exporter connection pooling / HTTP2 multiplexing" and linked from the doc.

infra-bot: ticket INF-9836 created by maya at 2027-11-03T23:40:09Z

maya: closing this thread for now — watch the dashboard and ping if anything spikes again. last metrics at 23:41 show canary healthy."
